findings.reason: the §4 eight-beat coordination and the "migrate the ambix geometry source and identity tests" done-when are sized for a test-only coupling; a production reader must migrate first and the inventory row is wrong.
findings.text: the plan's §3 "cross-repo" row names only ambix *test* files (`tests/gs/test_machine_identity.py`, `tests/gs/test_artifact_resolution.py`), but the live dependency is a production import: `author_pinned_description()` calls `nova.imas.mast_geometry.publish_refined_artifact` (a module §3 marks "retires"), and `_resolve_stored()`/`_semantic_identity_of()` call `nova.imas.machine_artifact.{resolve_machine_artifact,MachineArtifactManifest}` at lines 171/268 — so a deletion here breaks ambix's runtime geometry route, not just its test suite, which changes the cutover sequencing the plan assumes.

findings.reason: the plan's core premise ("replaces all three generically") fails for the cache/publish third, so the design needs either to keep the owner and expose it, or to name the ambix module that genuinely re-implements it.
findings.text: the plan re-homes the machine-generic publication capability (`latest_publication_dd_version()` / `publication_dd_version()`) into the producer, but that function already lives in and is used by the live DIII-D route (`nova/scripts/diiid_machine_artifact.py:349`); ambix's only "replacement" candidate, `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py`, does not implement any of it and instead forwards to nova's `materialize_machine_artifact` (its own docstring at lines 38–40 says so), so the re-home copies a capability into a second repository rather than replacing it and the plan never states why the owner cannot simply be extended in place.

findings.reason: the re-home inventory is under-counted by exactly the copy the live DIII-D publication path touches, and the plan would retire the one floor it names while leaving a second, unmentioned duplicate serving the live DIII-D path.
findings.text: the plan's §2/§3 speak of "the DDv4 publication floor" as a single owner-directed capability to re-home, but nova already carries two implementations of it: `latest_publication_dd_version()` (PUBLISHED major 4) at `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:115`, and `latest_published_dd_version()` (PUBLISHED_DD_MAJOR = 4) here at line 36, used at line 679 in the same module.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new module in nova; its design retires surface rather than adding an abstraction with a hidden interior, so there is no new deep/shallow module to judge (the re-home's placement is scored under thin_wrapper and duplicate_owner).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the DDv4 publication floor the plan treats as one capability to re-home already exists twice in nova, at `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:115` and `nova/imas/diiid_machine_ids.py:36`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched `imas-ambix` only through its test files, and missed the production module that carries the real cross-repo coupling, `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan re-homes nova's publication capability "into the producer" without saying why the owner `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py` cannot simply be extended, and the receiving ambix module is itself a forwarding wrapper over nova rather than a replacement.
